title: Runtime hardware profile pack rollout checklist (SRE working doc)
content:
Context
- This is the SRE working checklist for rolling out the “hardware tuning profiles pack” in runtime-1.22.
- Audience: SRE on-call, runtime on-call, release engineer, and infra duty.
- Applies to Hosted first (staged canary), then Dedicated opt-in, then Private guidance.

Definitions / shorthand
- profile pack: versioned set of per-SKU runtime tuning defaults (H100, L40S, B200 preview)
- profile_id: the selected profile within a pack (e.g., h100_sxm_prod_v1)
- profile_version: the version of the pack artifact (e.g., 1.0.0, 1.0.1)
- cohort: a set of instances/pools/endpoints receiving the new default
- “kill switch”: global disable of profile pack selection (fallback to legacy defaults)

Owners / escalation
- SRE primary: Rafael Mendes (rollout), Sean Gallagher (safety gates)
- Runtime primary: Sofia Ivanova (scheduler), Hiro Tanaka (kernel), Omar El-Sayed (KV/memory + metrics)
- Infra: Irene Choi (fleet constraints), Neha Kapoor (exec escalation)
- Release: Connor O’Brien (train/go-no-go)

Rollout prerequisites (must be true before any canary starts)
[ ] Release train readiness
    - [ ] runtime-1.22 RC deployed to staging + at least one production shadow pool
    - [ ] /health and debug endpoint show active profile_version + profile_id (ref: PR-25014)
    - [ ] Config flag path documented + verified (where kill switch lives; who can flip it)

[ ] Observability ready (dashboards exist + data is flowing)
    - [ ] “Runtime Profiles” overview dashboard is published and accessible to SRE + runtime on-call (ref: observability-pack/pr-221)
    - [ ] Latency histograms tagged with sku + profile_id (ref: PR-24935)
    - [ ] scheduler_queue_ms metric present and non-null in production for at least 24h on baseline cohort
    - [ ] kernel_choice / fallback counters present for H100 pools
    - [ ] OOM + allocator/fragmentation signals visible (at minimum: OOM count, restart count, GPU memory high-water)

[ ] Alarms configured (paging vs ticket)
    Paging alarms (page SRE on-call):
    - [ ] p99 end-to-end latency regression gate (by route/model tier) exceeds threshold for 10m
    - [ ] elevated 5xx rate (runtime) above threshold for 5m
    - [ ] OOM/restart storm in canary cohort
    - [ ] hard kernel fallback spike correlated with latency regressions

    Ticket/heads-up alarms (create ticket + Slack heads-up):
    - [ ] sustained increase in scheduler_queue_ms p95 in canary
    - [ ] sustained drop in tokens/sec or GPU util (possible mis-tuning)
    - [ ] fragmentation estimate trending upward (if available) without OOM yet

[ ] Safety/rollback mechanisms verified
    - [ ] Kill switch tested end-to-end in staging: “new defaults on” -> “off” returns behavior to baseline
    - [ ] profile_version pin override tested (Dedicated-like behavior): ability to pin to prior version + confirm via debug endpoint
    - [ ] Rollback does not require binary downgrade (preferred: config-level rollback)

[ ] Canary gating integrated
    - [ ] perf-canary job compares new default vs baseline and posts result (ref: perf-canary/pr-388)
    - [ ] Define explicit go/no-go gates (see “Gates” section)
    - [ ] Agree on what’s “warn only” vs “block” for the first week of rollouts


Canary plan (Hosted)
Goal: ramp adoption while minimizing blast radius and ensuring we catch tail-latency regressions under mixed workloads.

Cohort design
- Cohort 0: internal shadow / low-traffic pools (if available)
- Cohort 1: 1% of Hosted traffic, limited to a single region + known-stable model set
- Cohort 2: 5% multi-region, include at least one “long context” workload bucket
- Cohort 3: 25% broad mix (region/model), includes highest-volume routes
- Cohort 4: 100% Hosted default

Cohort selection requirements
[ ] Each cohort includes:
    - [ ] At least one pool per primary SKU in production (H100 and L40S; B200 only if explicitly approved)
    - [ ] A mix of prompt/response length distributions (short, medium, long)
    - [ ] A “mixed workload” pool where concurrent prefill + decode are typical

[ ] Exclusions (explicit):
    - [ ] Do not include newly onboarded enterprise tenants in early cohorts
    - [ ] Do not include pools with known driver/CUDA drift unless explicitly covered by compatibility matrix

Ramp schedule (default; adjust based on gates)
- Cohort 0: 24h
- Cohort 1: 12–24h
- Cohort 2: 24h
- Cohort 3: 24–48h
- Cohort 4: after 48h stable + sign-offs

Required sign-offs to progress past Cohort 2
[ ] SRE on-call (or SRE lead on duty)
[ ] Runtime on-call
[ ] Infra duty (confirm no concurrent fleet maintenance that will confound metrics)


Gates (what blocks rollout)
Use this as the decision rubric. If something is ambiguous, bias towards stop/hold and gather evidence.

Hard block (automatic stop + rollback candidate)
- p99 end-to-end latency regression > 8% vs baseline (same route/model bucket) sustained 10m+ in canary
- p95 end-to-end latency regression > 10% sustained 15m+ in canary
- 5xx error rate increase > 0.15% absolute sustained 5m+ (or >2x baseline if baseline is very low)
- OOM/restart count increases materially (>= 2x baseline) or any restart storm pattern
- Kernel fallback rate exceeds “expected” band (H100):
  - e.g., fallback events/request > 0.02 sustained 15m OR sudden step-function increase coincident with latency

Soft block (pause ramp; investigate; proceed only with runtime + SRE agreement)
- scheduler_queue_ms p95 increases > 20% without corresponding traffic increase
- tokens/sec drops > 5% (unless explained by quality constraints or other known changes)
- GPU util decreases unexpectedly (possible under-batching / admission control too strict)
- Fragmentation estimate trending upward + memory headroom shrinking (even without OOM yet)

Notes
- Always compare canary vs matched control pools in same region + similar traffic.
- If an upstream customer traffic shift occurred, annotate in the rollout log before making decisions.


Dashboards to watch (minimum set)
(These are the exact links SRE should keep open during ramp; add URLs in the final version of this doc.)

1) Runtime Profiles – Overview
- Adoption: % traffic by profile_version/profile_id
- Latency p50/p95/p99 by profile_id and SKU
- Kernel fallback counters (H100)
- scheduler_queue_ms p50/p95

2) API/Route Latency – Top routes
- p95/p99 for top 10 routes (and top customer-specific routes if applicable)
- Split by region + model family

3) Error Rates
- 4xx vs 5xx; timeouts separately if available
- Runtime internal errors (OOM, CUDA errors, allocator errors)

4) GPU + Memory
- GPU mem used high-water, utilization, power/clock anomalies if available
- Restart counts by pool

5) KV Cache / Memory Stability
- KV cache hit rate (if surfaced)
- Compaction time + compaction count (if surfaced)
- Fragmentation estimate / allocator pressure metrics (if surfaced)


Alarm tuning notes (early rollout)
- Expect some level of kernel fallback on edge workloads; do not page solely on “any fallback.” Page on correlation with tail latency or step-changes.
- Beware cardinality: keep alerts aggregated by sku + profile_version (not per-host) unless debugging.


Rollback playbook
Rollback levels (preferred order)
L0: Pause ramp
- Stop increasing cohort percentage.
- Keep current canary % if impact is not severe, while investigating.

L1: Roll back default profile_version (Hosted)
- Flip Hosted fleet default back to previous profile_version.
- Keep customer pins intact.
- Verify via:
  - /health shows old profile_version
  - Dashboard: adoption shifts back within 10–20 minutes (depending on rollout mechanism)

L2: Kill switch (disable profile pack)
- Disable profile pack selection globally (revert to legacy defaults).
- Use when:
  - Unknown failure mode
  - Metrics are missing/inconsistent
  - Rollback-by-version fails or is too slow

L3: Binary rollback
- Only if necessary (e.g., selection logic bug, crash loop)
- Coordinate with Release Eng (Connor) + Runtime

Rollback verification checklist
[ ] Within 30m, canary/control deltas return to baseline trend
[ ] OOM/restart rate returns to baseline
[ ] Kernel fallback returns to baseline
[ ] Confirm no lingering profile pins causing partial rollback

Post-rollback actions
[ ] Open incident or “near miss” ticket (depending on severity)
[ ] Snapshot dashboards + export key timeseries for investigation
[ ] File follow-ups (metrics gaps, gate thresholds, documentation updates)
[ ] Update rollout log with decision + timestamp + who approved


On-call communications template (Slack)
Channel: #eng-sre (and #eng-runtime for runtime-specific issues). For incidents, use #incidents.

Template: rollout start
---
[Runtime Profiles Pack] Starting canary rollout
- Change: enable profile pack defaults for Cohort X (Y% traffic)
- Scope: Hosted / Region(s): ___ / SKU(s): ___ / Model set: ___
- Profile version: ___ (previous: ___)
- Gates: p99 <= +8%, 5xx <= baseline+0.15%, no OOM increase
- Dashboards: Runtime Profiles Overview; Top Routes Latency; Errors; GPU/Memory
- Owners online: SRE ___, Runtime ___, Infra ___
- Next checkpoint: ___ UTC
---

Template: checkpoint update
---
[Runtime Profiles Pack] Canary checkpoint (Cohort X)
- Time window: ___ to ___ UTC
- Latency: p99 delta ___% (canary vs control), p95 delta ___%
- Errors: 5xx delta ___ (abs), timeouts ___
- Stability: OOM/restarts ___ (baseline ___)
- Kernel fallback: ___ (expected band: ___)
- Decision: proceed / hold / rollback
- Notes: traffic anomalies? deploys? fleet changes?
---

Template: rollback notice
---
[Runtime Profiles Pack] Rolling back
- Trigger: (gate violated) ___
- Action: L1 rollback to profile_version ___ (or L2 kill switch)
- Scope: Hosted cohort(s) ___
- Owners: SRE ___, Runtime ___
- ETA for verification: ___ minutes
- Link: incident/ticket ___
---

Template: Dedicated customer comms (internal summary for Support/CS)
---
Heads-up: performance profile change in runtime-1.22
- If customer reports regression, first step: confirm active profile_version/profile_id from debug bundle.
- Approved mitigation: pin customer to profile_version ___ (or disable profile pack for that tenant if supported).
- Escalate to: Runtime on-call + SRE on-call. Reference ticket: ___
---


Runbook: “customer says p99 got worse after upgrade” (fast triage)
1) Confirm whether the customer is in a canary cohort or pinned (profile_version/profile_id)
2) Compare the same time window vs a control pool
3) Check:
   - scheduler_queue_ms (queueing vs compute)
   - kernel fallback (H100)
   - OOM/restarts (especially L40S)
4) Mitigation options:
   - Pin to last known-good profile_version
   - Reduce concurrency cap (L40S) if stability-related
   - Roll back cohort if widespread
5) Capture:
   - customer_id, region, model, prompt/response lengths if known
   - timestamps + graphs


Open questions / TODOs (track before “final”)
- [ ] Finalize exact thresholds per SKU (H100 vs L40S may require different p99 gates)
- [ ] Confirm who has permissions to flip kill switch in production and document access path
- [ ] Add final URLs for dashboards + alert definitions
- [ ] Document Dedicated opt-in workflow (who approves pins, audit log location)
- [ ] Add B200 preview policy (default: never auto-enable; require explicit profile_version + compatibility gate)

Change log (manual)
- 2026-02-06: Added rollback levels + verification checklist.
- 2026-02-12: Added kernel fallback paging guidance and cohort requirements.
- 2026-02-21: Added on-call templates and fast triage runbook; marked doc in_review.
